scope: Records the first matched Optane cold-KV control on B550: the same model, the same 8192-token real-source prompt, the same engine and the same seed, with the cold tier off and then on, plus the counters the engine reported for the cold arm. It does not claim the cold tier is faster, does not claim it saves RAM, and does not cover the 600K or 800K scale gates.

hardware.gpus: 2 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, compute capability 8.6
hardware.engine_build: CUDA sm_86, release, portable, from the pinned llama.cpp 3cf03257

cold_device.smart: PASSED, 0% used, 0 media and data integrity errors, 0 error log entries
cold_device.note: The device's mode is synthesized by exFAT from dmask, so a 0700 directory is unreachable there; the privacy property that does hold is that other users cannot write the tier.

prompt.source: real source files on the host (salm-lora prompts.py, sweep_salm.py, build_error_mass.py, bench_rollout_e2e.py, build_vision_pack.py), tokenized with the pack's own tokenizer files
prompt.note: A fixed seed, because the draft acceptance path samples.

findings: The cold tier is genuinely in the serving path: 24,660 graph-split windows, 24,660 selection, readiness and resolve phases, and zero split violations.
The tier's bytes reach the copy the attention reads: 794,873 engine host restores.
Cold reads really happened: 756,560 L2 reads totalling 102,262,702,080 bytes, with 756,560 L1 evictions and zero read failures and zero checksum errors.
The outputs are bit-identical: the same 16 output token ids, the same 8,191 scored positions, a mean NLL delta of exactly 0.0 and a maximum absolute log-probability delta of exactly 0.0.
The cold arm is much slower for this workload: the prompt read took 1,086,512.9 ms against 73,222.8 ms without the tier, about 14.8x, and the decode took 7,049.2 ms against 243.3 ms, about 29x.

The slowdown is the tier's own accounting, not a fault: with 8 L1 groups per layer and a working set of 768 published groups, 756,560 of 794,873 group reads missed the cache and came from the device, and each one waited for the readiness phase.

One defect was found and fixed by this gate: the coordinator published an FNV-1a checksum while the file store verified with its own CRC-32, so every group read back from a store was refused. The tiers now share one checksum function.
non_claims: The cold tier is NOT faster here: it is about 14.8x slower on the prompt read and about 29x slower on the decode for this workload. No speed benefit is claimed.
The engine's pinned host allocation is not reduced: the tier's restore path repopulates the copy the attention reads, so the RAM-saving goal is still not met.
The L1 group cache was deliberately small (8 groups per layer) to force cold reads; a larger L1 would trade device reads for host memory, and that trade was not measured.
The 8192-token prompt is far shorter than the 262,144-cell context, so the tier's behaviour at a long context is not covered.
The Optane-class name of the device is unverified: it is recorded as HPE OEM Intel ET000750KWJTF, and the live SMART read does not state whether the media is 3D XPoint.
The device is exFAT, so the tier's files carry no POSIX permissions; the tier's directory mode is synthesized from the mount's dmask.

The sm86 identity gate still reports a difference: with the sm86 performance stack on and off, the teacher-forced log-probabilities are bit-identical over 511 scored positions, but one generated token differs at position 11, because the two arms take different expert-arithmetic paths. That gate is a separate claim and it did not pass.
